voiceover: Entry ten. Everyone's taking photos. Where do they go? Norah's Notebook, entry ten. The story is fiction. The fix is real. Last time: the sun set, the room glowed, and everyone took photos. Dear notebook: the day after. Mara's phone won't stop buzzing. Wedding photos arrive in group chats. More are still on cameras. WhatsApp usually compresses the photos you send. Its own help page says so. Zoom in on a group shot, and the details blur. Eli's cousin Dana says: just use iPhone photo sharing. It holds a hundred people at most. Mara and Eli have one hundred and eight names. And not every guest has an iPhone. Here's the part people skip: wedding guest photo sharing needs one clear place. Say it where guests already look: the welcome sign, table cards, signs, thank-you notes. Wedillybird gives guests one place to add photos: the same link as their invitation. Photos are screened automatically, and you approve or reject. Nothing to install, nothing to sign up for. The gallery stays open after the wedding, but not forever. Planning a winter wedding? Follow along. Tomorrow: check your invitation on a guest's phone. Mara writes one line on every thank-you card. Open your invitation link and add your photos. Ten entries. Ten problems crossed out. A spreadsheet. A group chat. A maybe. A plus-one. A stranger. A headcount. A door. A signal. A sunset. A pile of photos. I'm Norah, an AI character, and this is Wedillybird. The pen crosses out the photos, and writes the last line. Everyone's taking photos. Now they know where to send them. Season one done. Follow for what's next. And see a sample invitation: link in bio.

wedding guest photo sharing

Fiction: Norah and the couple are invented. The tips are real.
Hosted by Norah, an AI character created by the Wedillybird team.
pinned_comment:
Entry 10 recap, season one finale (the story is fiction, the tips are real):
1. WhatsApp usually compresses the photos you send (WhatsApp Help Center), and zoomed-in group shots can blur (dpa via The Star, 2024).
2. iPhone photo sharing holds at most 100 people (Apple Support, September 2026), and not every guest has an iPhone.
3. Pick one place for guest photos and say it where guests already look: the welcome sign, table cards, day-of signs and thank-you notes (Joy).
Want to see a sample invitation? Link in bio.
Fiction: Norah and the couple are invented. Norah is AI-generated. Screens shown are real Wedillybird screens (demo data).
comment_bait: Where do you want your guests' photos to end up?

sources.fact: Photos and videos shared through WhatsApp are usually compressed, which can look blurry, grainy or pixelated; an HD option exists but is chosen when sending
sources.title: How to send media (r2 read via search extract; direct fetch returned a script shell)

sources.fact: The app drastically compresses photos so details blur when zoomed, especially in group photos
sources.title: How to send WhatsApp photos in HD

sources.fact: iPhone photo sharing is capped at 100 people: up to 100 subscribers (created in iOS 26 or earlier) or up to 100 participants including the owner (version 27 or later)
sources.title: iCloud shared photo limits (page published 2026-09-14)

sources.fact: Place the photo-sharing instruction where guests already look: a venue welcome sign, table cards or favor tags, day-of signage; label it, print the web address under any code, use a permanent address and a mobile-friendly page
sources.title: What Is a Wedding QR Code?

numbers_used.figure: a hundred people at most (iPhone photo sharing)
numbers_used.source: Apple Support, iCloud shared photo limits, published 2026-09-14

needs_proof: S10 capture must come from the seeded stack: a guest adds a photo from the invitation link and the couple approves or rejects (demo data, stock or AI images, no real faces; r3 F1 row 7). Do not film upload speed or face search. If unavailable, replace the two SCREEN beats with a title card 'Guests add photos from their invitation link. You approve what appears.': the voice-over alone carries the meaning.

The gallery window depends on the plan (r3 B3), so the voice-over says 'not forever' and gives no duration. Founder: confirm the thank-you-card line is acceptable for plans whose window may have closed.
Founder: confirm a guest can reopen the gallery later from the same invitation link while the window is open (r3 B3).

T54 is confidence medium (mechanisms sourced, the 'scatter' is analysis): only WhatsApp's own compression statement and the dpa blur remark are used; no participation statistic. The thank-you-card spot comes from T57 supporting point 3 (Joy help page, vendor advice, search extract).
Re-check Apple's limits page before posting: both versions cap at 100 people, but the rules differ by iOS version.
claims_review.notes: Fiction: the wedding, the buzzing phone, Eli's cousin Dana (from entry 04) and the season recap are story elements; 'one hundred and eight names' is the guest count that entry 05 ends on. The final lines recap the story, they are not results. No scannable-code feature is mentioned or implied: the gallery opens from the guest's own invitation link, and the four places to 'say it' are spoken as advice for any photo-sharing method. Product beat is S10 only (about 9 s on screen): guests add photos from the same link, photos are screened automatically, the couple approves or rejects, nothing to install; no speed, quality, storage, price or face-search claim. The gallery compresses uploads in the browser (r3 B3), so no full-quality claim is made. WhatsApp and Apple appear as third-party apps cited as sources, not compared with Wedillybird. Season-one close uses the bible's wording (Season one done. Follow for what's next.) after the series ritual: AI line, pen line, closing lines; the follow CTA with the next-video teaser sits mid-video.
